lines.say: An inequality compares two amounts that might not be equal.
A ride says: you must be 120 centimetres or taller.
120 works. So do 121, 135.5 and 180.
So one rule gives a whole range of answers. A number line shows them all.
Less than, and greater than.
Less than or equal to, and greater than or equal to.
The line underneath is half an equals sign. So the end number is included.
The small pointed end faces the smaller number.

draw.alt: 3 < 8: the point of the sign faces the smaller number; x < 4 is the same as 4 > x

lines.say: x less than 4 says the same as 4 greater than x.
Show x greater than 2. Put a circle on the boundary, 2.

draw.alt: Number line: x > 2, open circle at 2, arrow to the right

lines.say: 2 itself doesn't work, so the circle is open. Hollow.
Greater means bigger numbers. Draw the arrow to the right.

draw.alt: Number line: x > 2, open circle at 2, arrow to the right

lines.say: Any number counts, not just whole ones. 2.1 and 1000 both work.
Now x is less than or equal to minus 1. Minus 1 works.

draw.alt: Number line: x ≤ −1, closed circle at −1, arrow to the left

lines.say: So the circle is closed. Filled with the number.
Less means smaller numbers. The arrow points left.

draw.alt: Number line: x ≤ −1, closed circle at −1, arrow to the left

lines.say: Test a number. Minus 3 is on the arrow, and it is less than minus 1.
Minus 2 is less than x, which is less than or equal to 3.

draw.alt: Number line: −2 < x ≤ 3, open circle at −2, closed at 3, joined

lines.say: Open circle at minus 2. Closed circle at 3. Join them.

draw.alt: Number line: −2 < x ≤ 3, open circle at −2, closed at 3, joined

lines.say: Only whole numbers? List them. Try minus 3 up to, but not including, 1.

draw.alt: Number line: −3 ≤ x < 1 with the integers −3, −2, −1, 0 highlighted

lines.say: The integers are minus 3, minus 2, minus 1 and 0.

draw.alt: Number line: −3 ≤ x < 1 with the integers −3, −2, −1, 0 highlighted

lines.say: Open circle at 5, arrow pointing left. What's the inequality?
lines.alt: Number line from 0 to 8 with an open circle at 5 and an arrow pointing left

lines.say: Boundary is 5. Open circle, so less than or greater than.
Arrow points left, so smaller. x is less than 5.
Words too. No more than 12 degrees means 12 or less.
Filled circle means the number is in. Open means it's out.
x greater than minus 4 still points right. Greater is always right.
4 greater than x means x is less than 4.
Don't forget decimals. x less than 3 includes 2.99.
Line under, number's in. That means a filled circle.

draw.alt: Number line: x ≤ −1, closed circle at −1, arrow to the left

lines.say: No line under? Open circle.

draw.alt: Number line: x > 2, open circle at 2, arrow to the right

lines.say: Right is greater, left is less. Then test a number.
